chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has land from the tax-land, and he hands it over to another man on the condition that he cultivates it, improves it, and pays its tax, and whatever surplus there is, it is shared between them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who gives his land to another man, and therein are pomegranates, or palm trees, or fruit, so he says: 'Irrigate this with the water and cultivate it, and for you is half of what is produced.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who gives the land to another man, so he says: 'Cultivate it and it is for you for three years, or five years, or whatever Allah wills.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about al-muzāraʿah (sharecropping), so he said: 'The expenditure is for you, and the land is for its owner. So whatever Allah brings out from it of anything, it is divided upon the half. And thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) give the people of Khaybar when they came to him, so he gave it to them on the condition that they cultivate it, and for them is half of what it produces.'

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْخَرَاجِ: Tax-land / Governmental land subject to tribute
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله وسل: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible conditions for agricultural sharecropping (muzāraʿah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of *muzāraʿah* (agricultural sharecropping) by validating flexible contracts where the cultivator bears operational costs (*nafaqah*) while the landowner retains ownership, with produce shared equally. It grounds this juristic ruling in the historical precedent of the Prophet Muhammad granting Khaybar to its inhabitants, a key event in Shia and Sunni legal tradition regarding land tenure and revenue sharing. The text clarifies that such arrangements are valid whether the share is fixed at half or determined by mutual agreement, emphasizing practical economic justice in agrarian societies.
